newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong to stay int'l trade centre--Bnk of China.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong to stay int'l trade centre--Bnk of China.

text.p: Hong Kong could raise its status as an international trading centre despite the challenges it faces, the Bank of China said on Tuesday in a research report.

The transfer of sovereignty from Britain to China next year, the improvement in China's trade facilties and capability, and the opening up of direct traffic links between China and Taiwan were all problems the territory could cope with, the bank said.
Hong Kong has long functioned as an entrepot for China and an intermediary for trade between China and Taiwan. Re-exports account for a significant proportion of total exports.
The British colony reverts to China in mid-1997, but the territory's trade regime and policies would stay unchanged after handover, the report said.
While China's improving trade facilties and capability would mean some competition, Hong Kong would still see increasing China-related trade, it added.

That was partly because the transportation links between Hong Kong and China were also improving, while Hong Kong and overseas entrepreneurs engaged in processing industries in China would still rely on Hong Kong for sourcing and marketing.
Direct traffic links between China and Taiwan would need time to develop, the bank said.
Hong Kong's trade and transportation links with Taiwan and southern and western China were efficient, it added.

Anticipated growth in international trade would benefit Hong Kong, with its strategic geographic location, natural habour, free and open policy, good communications network and adequate financial services, the report said.
